# weathernext-parser fixtures

Everything in this directory is SYNTHETIC and is regenerated byte-for-byte by
`generate-fixtures.mjs` (no randomness, no clock). `expected.json` in each
subdirectory is computed by the generator from the same closed-form field the
chunk bytes are written from, so a parser test compares against arithmetic,
never against another parser's output.

## wn3-0p1deg-clouds/

Layout facts taken from the developer model page (0.1 degree gridded surface
variables; `low_cloud_cover`, `medium_cloud_cover`, `high_cloud_cover` are
cover fractions in [0, 1]) and the WeatherNext 3 paper (0.1 degree global grid,
1801 latitudes x 3600 longitudes):

- `<array>.zarr.json`: Zarr v3 array metadata (`zarr_format` 3, `node_type`
  array, shape `[1, 64, 361, 1801, 3600]`, `data_type` float32, regular chunk
  grid `[1, 1, 1, 64, 64]`, default chunk-key encoding with `/` separator,
  `fill_value` NaN, codecs `[bytes(little)]`, dimension names
  `init_time, member, lead_time, latitude, longitude`, attributes
  `units: "1"`).
- `<array>.zstd.zarr.json`: identical, codecs `[bytes(little), zstd(level 3,
  no checksum)]`.
- `<array>.c.0.0.6.14.7.bin`: one full 64 x 64 float32 little-endian chunk
  (init 0, member 0, lead index 6 = 6 h, latitude chunk 14 = rows 896..959,
  longitude chunk 7 = columns 448..511).
- `low_cloud_cover.c.0.0.6.28.7.bin`: the array-edge chunk (latitude chunk 28
  = rows 1792..1800, nine real rows, the remaining 55 rows NaN fill; still
  16384 bytes).
- `*.zst`: the same chunks compressed with `node:zlib` `zstdCompressSync`
  (level 3, checksum off).

Cell value for layer L (low 0, medium 1, high 2) at cell centre
`phi = 90 - 0.1 i`, `lambda = 0.1 j` (degrees, global indices):

    v = clamp(0.5 + 0.5 sin((lambda + 20 L) pi/180 (2 + L))
                   cos((phi - 10 L) pi/180 (3 + L)), 0, 1)

computed in double then rounded to float32 (`Math.fround`). Medium layer only:
cells with `(i mod 64)` in 30..32 and `(j mod 64)` in 30..32 are NaN (nine
cells per chunk).

`expected.json` records, per chunk file: sha256, byte length, decoded
NLAT / NLON / LAT0 / LON0 / DLAT / DLON / PERIODIC_LON, TILE_INDEX
(`14 * 57 + 7 = 805`; edge `28 * 57 + 7 = 1603`), TILE_COUNT (`29 * 57 =
1653`), VALUE_MIN, VALUE_MAX, MISSING_COUNT, and spot cells at local
(0, 0), (63, 63), (31, 17) (edge chunk: (8, 63)), plus the zstd twin's sha256.

## UNVERIFIED against the live store

The real chunk shape, codec chain and dimension order of
`gs://weathernext3_spatial` are UNVERIFIED: anonymous reads of the bucket
returned 401/403 on 2026-09-03 (access is allow-listed). That is exactly why
chunk shape, codecs, dimension order, dtype and the store path are
operator-declared configuration on the live path and job JSON here, and why
the parser validates every chunk by size (`product(chunk_shape) * itemsize`)
rather than trusting a hardcoded layout.

## wn3-cyclones/

`cyclone-tracks.csv`: RFC 4180 (CRLF, header row) with the columns
`storm_id, storm_name, basin, track_origin, init_time, member, valid_time,
lead_hours, latitude, longitude, existence_probability,
max_sustained_wind_kt, min_central_pressure_hpa, radius_max_wind_nmi,
r34_{ne,se,sw,nw}_nmi, r50_{ne,se,sw,nw}_nmi, r64_{ne,se,sw,nw}_nmi`.
Two storms (`2026245N12300` "ALPHA", North Atlantic, existing system;
`2026248N15290`, unnamed, North Atlantic, genesis) x members 0, 1, 2 x leads
0, 6, 12, 18, 24 h from init 2026-09-02T00:00:00Z = 30 rows. Values are
hand-set and plausible: blank radii (not reported), zero r64 radii (threshold
not reached), a storm crossing the 34 kt and 64 kt category boundaries, a
longitude in [0, 360) form that must normalise to [-180, 180), and rows
deliberately written out of time order (6, 0, 18, 12, 24 h) so a parser must
sort points by valid time.

`expected.json` lists, per (storm, member): point count, first/last
VALID_TIME_MS, every converted point (Vmax m/s = `fround(kt * 1852 / 3600)`,
Pmin Pa = hPa * 100, radii km = `fround(nmi * 1.852)`, blank -> -1, category
from Vmax m/s, existence probability, blank -> 1), TRACK_ORIGIN, and the CSV
sha256 / byte length.
